customers.name: Multichannel Merchant Owner
customers.description: Owner or managing director of a Dutch or Belgian webshop, retailer or wholesaler with roughly EUR 0.3m to 30m annual revenue that sells through its own webshop and one or more marketplaces (bol, Amazon, Kaufland, Decathlon, MediaMarkt). Signs the EffectConnect subscription, decides which marketplaces and countries to enter, and judges the integrator on margin, reliability and support. Often already runs a Katapull back office such as Logic4 or Vendit.
careAbout: Marketplace revenue that is profitable after commission, fees and shipping
Not hiring extra staff for each new marketplace
A partner that answers the phone in Dutch when bol changes something
Predictable software cost instead of a percentage of revenue
winsThem: A fixed monthly subscription with no revenue commission
Proof from peers in the same sector (sports, tools, garden, electronics)
Go-live in weeks via a plugin for the webshop or back office they already use
A team that configures the setup with them
theirFear: Being suspended by bol or Amazon for cancellations or late shipments
Selling stock that is not there during a peak
Integrations that break silently after a marketplace API change
Locking into an integrator that charges more as they grow

customerJourneyStories.name: Switching integrator after the back office drops its own bol link
customerJourneyStories.summary: A sports retailer whose back office stops supporting its own bol connection moves to EffectConnect and expands to Amazon and Kaufland.

stages.narrative: The back-office vendor announces it will phase out its own bol integration, or the current integrator raises fees as a percentage of revenue.
The owner hears of EffectConnect from the Logic4 or Vendit account manager, the bol partner platform (Gold Partner listing) or a peer at Webwinkel Vakdagen.

Compares EffectConnect with ChannelEngine and Channable on price model (fixed fee versus commission), Dutch support and existing back-office connector; checks the published Platform price from EUR 305 per month and asks for references in the same sector.
Goes live on bol with the existing catalogue through the back-office connector, with an EffectConnect colleague configuring order flow and LVB stock rules in about two weeks.
Adds the repricer and a second marketplace, reviews the monthly reporting with the EffectConnect consultant and lets the team stop retyping orders.
Stays because marketplace revenue grows without new hires and the cost is fixed; expands to Scale with unlimited marketplaces and recommends EffectConnect to peers.

customerJourneyStories.name: Getting through peak season without oversells
customerJourneyStories.summary: An operations lead adopts real-time stock sync and the fulfilment manager after a painful peak.

stages.narrative: A Black Friday with oversold products, seller cancellations and a warning from bol about the cancellation rate.
Hears from the DeliveryMatch or Picqer account manager, or a Monta or Fulfilment.nl logistics partner, that EffectConnect connects marketplace orders and stock to their tools.
Checks with IT how orders and shipments will flow, whether multiple stock locations are supported and how LVB and FBA are handled; asks for a reference from a merchant with similar volumes.
Runs orders from one marketplace through the hub for a few weeks with stock buffers and the stock alarm switched on.
Uses the fulfilment console daily: LVB switch, replenishment shipments and exception queues; stock is pushed from several locations.
Stays because peak passes without penalties; asks for more marketplaces to be added through the same order flow.

careAbout: One stable, documented API instead of one per marketplace
Predictable behaviour under peak load and rate limits
Clear errors and monitoring of every sync
Access control and secure handling of marketplace credentials

Uniform order and product formats across marketplaces
Replacing several point-to-point connections

customerJourneyStories.summary: An integration lead replaces three self-built marketplace connections with the EffectConnect API.

stages.narrative: The Amazon and bol APIs both announce breaking changes in the same quarter and the in-house connectors need rework.
Reads the EffectConnect developer documentation and the 'for IT managers' page after the e-commerce manager shortlists integrators; sees OrderChief and other middleware connecting to it.
Reviews API documentation, authentication, rate limits and error handling; checks data processing terms for consumer order data and asks about support escalation to developers.
Builds the order and stock flows for one marketplace against the API and runs it in parallel with the old connector for a few weeks.
Moves catalogue and price flows to the hub, retires the old connectors and uses the integration monitor to follow failed jobs.
Stays because marketplace API changes are handled by EffectConnect and incidents are rare; adds new marketplaces without new code.
